rich_summary: At Draupadi’s swayamvara, many powerful kings attempt to string a massive bow and strike a difficult target but fail. Karna, formidable and confident, prepares to shoot, yet Draupadi publicly refuses to accept a "Suta" (charioteer’s son) as her husband, forcing him to withdraw despite his ability. Other renowned rulers such as Sisupala, Jarasandha, and Salya also fail to string the bow. When the Kshatriyas give up, Arjuna—disguised as a Brahmana—rises from among the Brahmins, provoking debate and skepticism among them. Calm and reverent, he salutes Shiva and remembers Krishna before effortlessly stringing the bow and shooting the target with five arrows. The arena erupts in divine and human celebration as Arjuna wins Draupadi, revealing both his unmatched skill and the hidden power of the Pandavas in exile.

highlight_spans.why: Draupadi’s public rejection of Karna marks a dramatic and controversial moment that shapes later tensions between Karna and the Pandavas.
The failures of mighty kings emphasize the near-impossible nature of the challenge and heighten the significance of the eventual success.
Arjuna rising from among the Brahmanas in disguise introduces suspense and highlights the theme that true greatness may appear in humble form.
Arjuna effortlessly strings the bow and strikes the target, the pivotal triumph that wins Draupadi and reveals his extraordinary mastery.
The jubilant reaction—divine flowers, music, and cheers—captures the emotional climax as Arjuna secures Draupadi’s hand.

top_scenes.scene_text: Arjuna, disguised as a Brahmana, calmly lifts the massive bow before a stunned assembly of kings and Brahmins in Draupadi’s swayamvara hall.
Draupadi firmly refuses Karna in the arena as he stands ready with the drawn bow, the gathered kings watching in tense silence.
Arjuna releases the arrows that pierce the target through the rotating mechanism as celestial flowers rain down and the crowd erupts in awe.
